:::{#exm-mahalanobis-special}
#### Mahalanobis distance for diagonal variance matrices

If $\matr{\covmat}$ is
[diagonal](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-diagonal-matrix)
with diagonal elements $\varpar_1, \ldots, \varpar_p$, all positive,
then $\matr{\covmat}^{-1}$ is diagonal with diagonal elements
$1/\varpar_1, \ldots, 1/\varpar_p$
(multiplying the two gives $\matr{I}_p$;
[matrix inverse](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-matrix-inverse)), so:

$$
\mahal(\vx)^2 = \sumip \frac{(x_i - \mean_i)^2}{\varpar_i}
$$

Two special cases:

- If $\matr{\covmat} = \matr{I}_p$,
  then $\mahal(\vx)^2 = \sumip (x_i - \mean_i)^2$,
  so the Mahalanobis distance is the ordinary (Euclidean) distance.
- If $\matr{\covmat} = \ss \matr{I}_p$,
  then $\mahal(\vx)$ is the Euclidean distance divided by $\sdpar$.

In general, each coordinate's difference is measured
in units of that coordinate's standard deviation.

:::
